operations — Discrete Differential Operators¶

Differential operators and derived quantities (gradient, divergence, vorticity, …) used by the fluid solver.

Extracted from solver.py so they can be maintained independently. All functions are standalone — they take explicit grid parameters (h, ndim, dx, dy, dz) instead of relying on self.

lilytorch.src.operations.compute_dpdx(p, h)[source]¶

Compute dp/dx via central difference (multiply-by-reciprocal).

lilytorch.src.operations.compute_dpdy(p, h)[source]¶

Compute dp/dy via central difference (multiply-by-reciprocal).

lilytorch.src.operations.compute_dpdz(p, h)[source]¶

Compute dp/dz (3-D only, multiply-by-reciprocal).

lilytorch.src.operations.gradient(var, h, ndim)[source]¶

Compute gradient(var) using multiply-by-reciprocal (CPU/GPU parity). 2-D → (dvar_dx, dvar_dy), 3-D → (dvar_dx, dvar_dy, dvar_dz).

lilytorch.src.operations.divergence(u, v, dx, dy, w=None, dz=None)[source]¶

Compute the divergence using multiply-by-reciprocal (CPU/GPU parity).

lilytorch.src.operations.normal_derivative(var, h, ndim, normal_x, normal_y, normal_z=None)[source]¶

Compute the normal derivative dvar/dn = n · ∇var.

lilytorch.src.operations.vorticity(u, v, h, ndim, w=None)[source]¶

Compute vorticity. 2-D: scalar omega = dv/dx - du/dy 3-D: magnitude |ω| = sqrt(ωx² + ωy² + ωz²)

lilytorch.src.operations.vorticity_components(u, v, w, h)[source]¶

Return the three signed vorticity components (omega_x, omega_y, omega_z) as a dict, plus the magnitude. Only meaningful in 3-D.

lilytorch.src.operations.strain_rate_magnitude(vel, h, ndim)[source]¶

Compute |S̄| = sqrt(2 * S_ij * S_ij) on the cell-centred grid.

Parameters:

  • vel (tuple of tensors (u, v) in 2-D or (u, v, w) in 3-D.)

  • h (float — uniform grid spacing.)

  • ndim (int — 2 or 3.)

Return type:

|S̄| tensor with same shape as vel[0]. Ghost cells are zero.

lilytorch.src.operations.smagorinsky_viscosity(vel, h, ndim, cs=0.1)[source]¶

Compute the Smagorinsky eddy viscosity ν_t = (Cs·Δ)² |S̄|.

Parameters:

  • vel (tuple of tensors — velocity components.)

  • h (float — uniform grid spacing (used as filter width Δ).)

  • ndim (int — 2 or 3.)

  • cs (float — Smagorinsky constant (typically 0.1–0.2).)

Return type:

ν_t tensor with same shape as vel[0].

lilytorch.src.operations.carreau_viscosity(vel, h, ndim, nu_0, nu_inf, lam, n, tau_y=0.0, rho=1000.0, nu_max=None)[source]¶

Compute Carreau (or Herschel-Bulkley–Carreau) viscosity field.

Without yield stress (tau_y = 0):

ν(γ̇) = ν_∞ + (ν_0 − ν_∞) · [1 + (λ·γ̇)²]^((n−1)/2)

With yield stress (tau_y > 0):

ν(γ̇) = τ_y / (ρ · max(γ̇, γ̇_min)) + ν_∞ + (ν_0 − ν_∞) · [1 + (λ·γ̇)²]^((n−1)/2)

The total viscosity is clamped to nu_max to guarantee diffusion CFL stability. When nu_max is None no clamping is applied (pure Carreau without yield stress is bounded by ν_0 anyway).

Parameters:

  • vel (tuple of tensors — velocity components (u, v) or (u, v, w).)

  • h (float — uniform grid spacing.)

  • ndim (int — 2 or 3.)

  • nu_0 (float — zero-shear-rate kinematic viscosity [m²/s].)

  • nu_inf (float — infinite-shear-rate kinematic viscosity [m²/s].)

  • lam (float — relaxation time [s].)

  • n (float — power-law index (< 1 for shear-thinning).)

  • tau_y (float — yield stress [Pa]. Default 0 (pure Carreau).)

  • rho (float — fluid density [kg/m³]. Only used when tau_y > 0.)

  • nu_max (float or None — hard upper bound on ν for CFL stability.)

Return type:

ν tensor (spatially varying kinematic viscosity) with same shape as vel[0].

lilytorch.src.operations.cross_product_2d(ax, ay, bx, by)[source]¶

Element-wise 2-D cross product (scalar result).

lilytorch.src.operations.cross_product_3d(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz)[source]¶

Element-wise 3-D cross product a × b.

Returns (cx, cy, cz) tensors.
